physics_goals.quote: designed to improve on the sensitivity of the prior generation of experiment by a factor of 50 or more
value: Detect or exclude weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) scattering off xenon nuclei
Improve on the previous generation of xenon dark matter experiments by a factor of 50 or more
Accumulate a 1,000 live day exposure with seven active tonnes of liquid xenon
Search for rare processes in xenon, including the neutrinoless double beta decay of 136Xe

summary.plain: LZ is a dark matter experiment a mile underground in South Dakota. It watches seven tonnes of liquid xenon for the tiny flash of light expected if a dark matter particle hits a xenon nucleus. It began taking data at the end of 2021 and has seen no such particle so far.
summary.technical: Second-generation G2 direct-detection experiment using a dual-phase xenon TPC with 7 active tonnes (5.5 t SR1 fiducial) in the Davis Cavern at SURF (~1480 m rock, ~4300 m.w.e.). SR1 (60 live days, Dec 2021 - May 2022) set a spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit of 9.2e-48 cm2 at 36 GeV/c2; the 4.2 tonne-year WS2024 analysis reached 2.2e-48 cm2 at 40 GeV/c2. The programme targets 1,000 live days and also searches for 136Xe double beta decay.

unique_capabilities.quote: Rejection of backgrounds is enhanced by a Xe skin veto detector and by a liquid scintillator Outer Detector loaded with gadolinium for efficient neutron capture and tagging.
value: Seven active tonnes of liquid xenon, the largest dual-phase xenon target built when it started operating
Triple veto: instrumented xenon skin, gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector and a water shield, under ~1480 m of rock
